title: Localizations of a polynomial ring over a field at maximal ideals have dimension n
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ an integer, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $\mathfrak M\subset P$ a maximal ideal. Then the localization $P_{\mathfrak M}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] has Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] $\dim(P_{\mathfrak M})=n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660), second sentence ('The dimension of k[x_1, ..., x_n]_m is n'); cited for this in the paragraph after Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field, line 35836)

mathlib_candidate.how: Not a leaf: line 120 gives only dim k[x_1..x_n] = dim k + n = n globally; line 80 (`Polynomial.height_eq_height_add_one`, [IsNoetherianRing R], P maximal in R[X] lying over p: P.height = p.height + 1) gives the one-variable step, and iterating it over k[x_1..x_{i}] -> k[x_1..x_{i+1}] (with the contraction of a maximal ideal again maximal, by the Nullstellensatz) and translating height to dim P_M (IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height, Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Height.lean:418) is a proof of several lines, not a specialization. Alternative route: dim P_M = dim P for the domain P by Algebra 00OS (node lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-local-ring) and dim P = n by line 120.
